title: Drought tolerance in staple crops
bottleneck: Drought is the single largest cause of yield loss worldwide, yet breeding for drought tolerance has delivered only incremental gains because tolerance is polygenic, environment-specific, and usually trades off against yield in good years — farmers won't plant a variety that underperforms when rains are normal. Genetics hasn't kept pace with a shifting climate that makes droughts more frequent where food insecurity is highest.
why_it_blocks: Each severe drought in a food-insecure region is a famine risk. Without tolerant varieties, climate change directly translates into hunger.
current_state: Drought-tolerant maize and other varieties show modest gains in trials; no breakthrough variety transforms rainfed agriculture. Drought-tolerant maize and other varieties show modest gains in trials; no breakthrough transforms rainfed agriculture.
